questions.question_text: Solve $\sin 52^{\circ}=\dfrac{19}{x}$, giving $x$ correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Multiplied $19$ by $\sin 52^{\circ}$, which is the method for an unknown in the numerator.
Divided by $\cos 52^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 52^{\circ}$.
Divided by $\tan 52^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin 52^{\circ}$.

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (A) at (2.320,0);\coordinate (B) at (0,0);\coordinate (C) at (0,2.240);\draw (A)--(B);\draw (B)--(C) node[midway,left] {$14\text{ m}$};\draw (C)--(A) node[midway,above right] {$x$};\coordinate (va) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(A)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(B)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$44^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.6cm,angle eccentricity=1.5] {angle=C--A--B};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Which equation correctly relates $x$ to the marked angle?

options.why: Used opposite over adjacent, treating $x$ as the adjacent side when $x$ is the hypotenuse.
Chose the correct ratio but inverted the fraction, putting the hypotenuse in the numerator.
Made both slips: used opposite over adjacent and then inverted the fraction as well.

questions.solution_text:
The $14$ m side is opposite the $44^{\circ}$ angle $(O)$ and $x$ is the hypotenuse $(H)$.
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{O}{H}$
$\sin 44^{\circ}=\dfrac{14}{x}$

questions.question_text:
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (B) at (1.890,0);\coordinate (C) at (1.890,3.709);\draw (A)--(B) node[midway,below] {$4.2\text{ m}$};\draw (B)--(C);\draw (C)--(A) node[midway,above left] {$x$};\coordinate (va) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(A)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(B)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$63^{\circ}$",angle radius=0.5cm,angle eccentricity=1.6] {angle=B--A--C};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
A guy wire is pegged to the ground $4.2$ m from the base of a vertical tower and makes an angle of $63^{\circ}$ with the ground. Find the length $x$ of the wire, correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Multiplied $4.2$ by $\cos 63^{\circ}$, giving a wire shorter than its own ground distance.
Divided by $\sin 63^{\circ}$, treating the $4.2$ m as the side opposite the angle.
Divided by $\tan 63^{\circ}$, which returns the height of the tower rather than the wire.

A zip line drops $9$ m in height and slopes at $14^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. Find its length $x$, correct to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Divided by $\tan 14^{\circ}$, which gives the horizontal distance instead of the sloping cable.
Multiplied $9$ by $\sin 14^{\circ}$, giving a cable shorter than the drop it spans.
Divided by $\cos 14^{\circ}$, treating the $9$ m drop as adjacent to the angle.

\begin{tikzpicture}\coordinate (A) at (0,0);\coordinate (B) at (3.100,0);\coordinate (C) at (3.100,3.371);\draw (A)--(B) node[midway,below] {$31\text{ cm}$};\draw (B)--(C);\draw (C)--(A) node[midway,above left] {$x$};\coordinate (va) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(A)$);\coordinate (vb) at ($(B)!0.3cm!(C)$);\draw (va)--($(va)+(vb)-(B)$)--(vb);\pic[draw,"$47^{\circ}24'$",angle radius=0.5cm,angle eccentricity=1.95] {angle=B--A--C};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Find $x$ correct to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Entered the angle as $47.24^{\circ}$, reading $24'$ as a decimal instead of $24$ sixtieths of a degree.
Divided by $\sin(47^{\circ}24')$, treating the $31$ cm side as opposite the angle.
Divided by $\tan(47^{\circ}24')$, which returns the third side rather than the hypotenuse.

questions.question_text: A student solving $\tan 71^{\circ}=\dfrac{58}{x}$ first writes $\tan 71^{\circ}\approx 2.9$, then $x=\dfrac{58}{2.9}=20.00$. What is the correct value of $x$, to $2$ decimal places?

options.why: Keeps the student's rounded $2.9$, so the rounded ratio is carried through into the answer.
Multiplied $58$ by $\tan 71^{\circ}$ instead of dividing by it.
Divided by $\sin 71^{\circ}$ instead of $\tan 71^{\circ}$.
